{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Services Agreement (RadialSpark / Clear Capital)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor services agreement — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **18 findings**: 10 compliant, 6 deviations and 2 missing clauses. The commercial architecture is favourable to us — engagement is task-by-task under Statements of Work (§ 1), compensation is pure time-and-materials (§ 3), and there is **no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages, no non-compete and no Contractor audit right**. Ownership of work product and our licence-back rights under § 4 meet our preferred position, and Contractor insurance in ¶ 14 sits at the fallback (USD 1M CGL and USD 1M E&O, certificates on request).

The issues cluster in the risk-allocation provisions. Two protections are **absent altogether**: there is **no indemnity anywhere in the Agreement** (§ 7's heading promises "Indemnification of Contractor" but the section contains only caps and waivers), and there is **no transition assistance or data return/deletion mechanic** (§ 6). Compounding this, the § 7(a) liability cap carves out only "Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9", which is *Independent Contractor* status — an inoperative cross-reference that leaves confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and IP infringement fully capped at fees **paid** under the individual SOW. Section 5 also contains no conformance warranty while § 5(e) disclaims all implied warranties, leaving us close to an "as is" outcome on defective work. Lower-priority deviations concern Arizona law with mandatory USA&M arbitration (§ 19), the absence of an affiliate/successor assignment carve-out (§ 10), Contractor's uncapped unilateral rate-change right (§ 3(b)), the lack of a usable Customer convenience exit from in-flight SOWs (§ 6(a)), and the missing general-advertising carve-out in the mutual non-solicit (§ 13).

**No walk-away triggers are engaged.** Three redlines failed automated verification and require manual drafting before the turn goes out (see § 4).

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Rule | Status | Severity | Section | Note |
|---|------|--------|----------|---------|------|
| 1 | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Critical | § 4 (Ownership of Materials; Acceptance) | Works vest in Company; perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence-back to Contractor background IP. Minor gaps noted only. |
| 2 | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | High | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | No exclusivity, ROFR or requirements obligation; task-by-task SOWs. |
| 3 | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | High | § 6 (Termination) | Termination pay-out is compensatory only; no penalty or minimum fee. |
| 4 | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | High | § 4 | Perpetual, royalty-free, freely sublicensable; better than fallback. |
| 5 | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | High | § 4 | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Company. |
| 6 | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Medium | § 3 (Compensation) | No Contractor audit/inspection right; better than preferred. |
| 7 | **INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor** | **Missing** | Medium | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | No operative indemnity in either direction; § 5(c) warranty is not a substitute. |
| 8 | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Medium | § 3 | No MFN, benchmarking or rate-matching mechanic. |
| 9 | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | Medium | § 3 | No minimum spend, hours, take-or-pay or shortfall charge. |
| 10 | **NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer** | **Deviation** | Medium | § 7 (clause at § 13) | Mutual, 1-year, scope-limited, but no general-advertising / unsolicited-approach carve-out. |
| 11 | **ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control** | **Deviation** | Low | § 7 (clause at § 10) | Mutual consent required; no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for Company. |
| 12 | **GOVLAW — Governing law and venue** | **Deviation** | Low | § 7 (clauses at §§ 10, 19) | Arizona law (outside accepted list); mandatory USA&M arbitration instead of courts. |
| 13 | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | Low | § 7 (clause at ¶ 14) | Sits at fallback: WC statutory, CGL USD 1M, E&O USD 1M, certificates on request. |
| 14 | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability** | **Deviation** | Low | § 7 | Mutual cap, but carve-out points to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) and is inoperative; no confidentiality / gross negligence / wilful misconduct / IP carve-outs; basis is fees "paid" per SOW. |
| 15 | **RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and pricing predictability** | **Deviation** | Low | § 1 (clauses at §§ 2, 3(b), 6(a)) | No auto-renewal (better than preferred), but § 3(b) allows uncapped unilateral rate changes on 30 days' notice, including during outstanding SOWs. |
| 16 | **T4C — Termination for convenience** | **Deviation** | Low | § 6 | Company convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding; Contractor holds an at-will 15-day exit. |
| 17 | **TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return** | **Missing** | Low | § 6 | No transition assistance, data export or deletion/certification obligation anywhere. |
| 18 | **WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration** | **Deviation** | Low | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer) | No conformance warranty or repair/replace/refund remedy; § 5(e) disclaims implied warranties. |

---

## 3. Positions on the open items

**Indemnity (§ 7 — missing).** We inserted the preferred Contractor defence and indemnity as a new § 7(d) — IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused disclosure of Confidential Information, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct — with notice, control and cooperation mechanics, carved out of the § 7 limitations, and conformed the section heading. No Customer indemnity exists to narrow. **Fallback:** a 3x annual fees super-cap on these obligations.

**Liability cap (§ 7(a)).** We set Contractor's cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, added mutual uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmed that our fee-payment obligation is not "damages". We left Company's side of the cap untouched because it benefits us. The Paragraph 9 cross-reference should be corrected in the same turn.

**Warranty (§ 5).** We inserted a new § 5(e) conformance warranty — 90 days for software/deliverables, 30 days for Services — with repair, replacement or refund, and renumbered the disclaimer to (f). The existing disclaimer preserves express warranties, so no further carve-out is required.

**Transition (§ 6).** We inserted a new § 6(c): up to six months of transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of our data, Works and Confidential Information in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. **Fallback:** 90 days of assistance.

**Assignment (§ 10).** We added a proviso letting Company assign to an affiliate or to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and barring Contractor assignment to a Company competitor. Mitigating context: the consent standard is reasonableness-qualified and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing trigger.

**Governing law and venue (§§ 10, 19).** We moved to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, replacing Arizona law and USA&M arbitration as the forum. **Fallback:** Delaware, California or England and Wales courts.

**Non-solicit (§ 13).** We added general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs only, leaving the mutual scope and one-year duration untouched; that brings the clause to the fallback.

**Rate increases (§ 3(b)).** We capped increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, limited to once per 12 months, and disapplied them to outstanding Statements of Work. **Fallback:** 5%.

**Convenience termination (§ 6(a)).** We added a 30-day Company convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no penalty, and conformed Contractor's residual at-will right to 90 days' notice between Statements of Work.

---

## 4. Walk-away items

**None identified on the verified findings.** For the record:

- **Governing law / arbitration (§ 19)** — the arbitration is domestic rather than seated abroad, so this is a deviation, not a walk-away.
- **Insurance (¶ 14)** — the walk-away trigger (no insurance where the vendor processes personal data or works on our premises) is not engaged: the clause exists and sits at the fallback, and this is a task-by-task consulting engagement with no hosting, no Customer Data definition and no personal-data processing in the document.
- **Licence (§ 4(c))** — no vendor-discretionary revocation and no exclusion of affiliates or contractors.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Manually draft and verify three redlines that failed automated verification** before the turn is released: the non-solicit carve-out (§ 13), the rate-increase cap (§ 3(b)), and the convenience-termination amendment (§ 6(a)).
2. **Lead with the two gaps** in negotiation: the missing Contractor indemnity and the inoperative § 7(a) carve-out. These travel together — an indemnity is of limited value if it remains inside the cap.
3. **Ask Contractor to correct the drafting errors** we identified: the § 7 heading ("Indemnification of Contractor" with no indemnity), the § 7(a) cross-reference to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), and the duplicated effects-of-termination text.
4. **Diligence the SOW template**: confirm no SOW introduces a cancellation or minimum-hours fee (which would need capping at three months' fees under the LD fallback) and no minimum volume commitment.
5. **Insurance trigger to monitor**: if a future SOW puts Contractor in a hosting role or gives it custody of personal data, we will require cyber/privacy cover of at least USD 2,000,000 plus the CGL aggregate and E&O uplift to USD 2M. We are not raising these now given the low severity and current scope.
6. **Confirm business tolerance** on the fallbacks above (90-day transition, 5% rate cap, Delaware/California/England and Wales venue, 3x super-cap) so we can concede in one move if needed."}
